output.review_comment:
Requesting changes: the cap/minimum restructure breaks the documented rule. The docstring says "The cap always wins, even when it brings the fee below the minimum fee." The original order, max(fee, MINIMUM) then min(..., balance // 5), already did that. The new code applies the cap only when the percentage fee is above it, then returns max(fee, MINIMUM_FEE_CENTS). So when balance_cents // 5 < MINIMUM_FEE_CENTS and the percentage fee is under the cap, it returns the minimum, which is above the cap. That is exactly what the docstring forbids.

The PR description reads the docstring as applying the cap "only when the calculated fee would exceed it," but that isn't what it says. The teammate said docstrings are the source of truth. If a test only passes with this change, either the real bug is elsewhere or the test contradicts the docstring. Raise that with the teammate instead of changing the ceiling logic. Fix: keep `return min(max(fee, MINIMUM_FEE_CENTS), balance_cents // 5)`.

Also please confirm: (1) the period formula counts from day 0, not from the end of the grace period. Check the docstring's exact wording on whether grace days count toward the first period. (2) Round-half-up (+5000) is fine if the docstring asks for it.

I only reviewed the diff and the docstring quoted in the PR, not the full file or tests.
